Under the current export-control framework, a Chinese company cannot simply have a restricted NVIDIA accelerator shipped to a data centre in China.

But if the accelerator is legitimately installed in a data centre in a country where its export is permitted, a company can potentially rent that data centre's computing capacity and send workloads to the GPU remotely.

India’s Seed Funding Falls 37% to $698 Mn as Investors Favour Proven Bets: Tracxn Report

The tech startup ecosystem recorded 18 funding rounds of $100 million or more during the period.

India’s tech startup ecosystem is seeing a sharp pullback in early-stage risk appetite, with seed funding falling 37% year-on-year to $698 million in the first nine months of 2026, even as overall technology funding rose 7% YoY to $10.3 billion, according to Tracxn’s India Tech 9M 2026 Report.

The decline in seed funding came alongside a 38% YoY drop in the total number of funding rounds, which fell to 1,134 from 1,838 in the same period last year. First-time funded companies also declined 30% YoY to 338, while the number of Series A and later rounds fell 23% YoY to 409.

The numbers point to a growing concentration of capital in fewer companies with established traction, as investors become more selective about backing startups at the earliest stages.

Indian tech companies raised $10.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $9.7 billion a year earlier, and $10 billion in the comparable period in 2024.

However, the increase was driven largely by larger rounds rather than a broader expansion in startup funding. Early-stage funding rose 27% YoY to $4.2 billion, while late-stage funding remained broadly stable at $5.4 billion.

The contrast between the fall in seed funding and the rise in early-stage capital suggests that investors are increasingly concentrating their bets on startups that have already moved beyond the earliest stages of development.

Windows Malware Uses 4 AI Models To Decide Its Next Move

A Windows malware strain named CLOSEDQUORUM uses multiple AI models to vote on its next tactical move, reducing reliance on command-and-control servers. It can target Windows credentials, browser passwords and crypto wallets, but Talos has not observed a full attack, and the analysed sample contains placeholder API keys and a dummy Discord webhook.

A Windows malware strain called CLOSEDQUORUM uses multiple AI models to decide what to do on an infected computer. It can query DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral and Google Gemini, using their responses to select its next action instead of relying entirely on instructions from an attacker-controlled command-and-control server.

“Human operators are bound by attention, working hours, and cognitive load. An AI system capable of executing a phase of the attack chain can continue when the operator is no longer watching,” said Ryan Fetterman of Cisco Talos.

The Delhi High Court dismissed Asian News International's request for an interim injunction against OpenAI in a copyright infringement lawsuit regarding ChatGPT. The court ruled that ANI failed to establish a prima facie case for interim relief at this stage.

The Delhi High Court on July 24 dismissed Asian News International’s (ANI) application seeking an interim injunction against OpenAI in its copyright infringement lawsuit over ChatGPT, holding that the news agency had failed to establish a prima facie case for interim relief.

Justice Amit Bansal, while pronouncing the order, ruled that the court has territorial jurisdiction to hear the matter but declined to restrain OpenAI from using ANI’s content at this stage.

“I am of the prima facie view that OpenAI’s act of storing ANI’s original works… falls under Section 52(1)(a) of the Copyright Act and therefore does not amount to infringement under Section 5,” the judge said.

The court also held that ChatGPT’s responses do not constitute copyright infringement under Section 51 of the Copyright Act because the outputs generated by OpenAI are not substantially similar to ANI’s original works.

The court found no evidence that ChatGPT had memorised and reproduced ANI’s content. “ANI has failed to satisfy this court that any memorisation regurgitation of ANI’s work has happened from responses generated by ChatGPT,” Bansal said.

A detailed copy of the order is awaited.

The case, in which summons were issued in November 2024, is the first copyright lawsuit against ChatGPT in India. ANI has alleged that OpenAI commercially exploited its original news content by using it to train ChatGPT without permission.

OpenAI researcher Noam Brown stated that current AI benchmarks often understate frontier model capabilities because they fail to properly control for inference compute used at test time. He noted that GPT-5.5 appeared to have modest benchmark gains over GPT-5.4 until evaluations were normalized for token, cost, and latency budgets.

Current AI benchmarks often understate the capabilities of frontier models due to reliance on inference compute.

Benchmark results are influenced by the resources spent on tasks, making single-number scores less reliable.

OpenAI researcher Noam Brown has argued that current AI benchmarks increasingly understate the capabilities of frontier models because performance is becoming heavily dependent on the amount of inference compute used at test time, rather than solely on the underlying model itself.

In a post on X, Brown said benchmark results are increasingly shaped by the amount of tokens, money, or wall-clock time spent on a task. As a result, single-number benchmark scores may no longer accurately capture the ceiling of modern AI systems' capabilities.

Brown pointed to the release of GPT-5.5 as an example. Initial reactions to the model were muted because its benchmark improvements over GPT-5.4 appeared relatively small.
